name: The Road In
description: Each player's small problem on the road, on a skill they name; and the violet mark, a free knowledge check.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: It goes better than it had any right to. Ask the player why it was worth remembering, and whatever they say is true from now on.
outcomes.failure: It doesn't quite work: they reach the city anyway, a bit late or a bit worse for wear.
outcomes.criticalFailure: It goes wrong in a way that is funny, not harmful, and they still reach the city.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: It isn't the first one they've seen: always this deep violet, always at head height, always where a crowd stops and waits. This one is fresh.
outcomes.success: Now they think about it, it isn't the first one today. The same deep violet, at the same height.
outcomes.failure: It looks like paint, and nothing more.
outcomes.criticalFailure: They are sure it's a condemned-building notice, the kind the housing office stencils on empty lots. It isn't, and nobody corrects them.

bySkill.occultism: Not idle graffiti. It was drawn in one unbroken stroke, carefully, the way you draw something that has to be right.
bySkill.crafting: Not house paint. It has the dull skin of marine primer, sold by the tin for ships' hulls, which is why the weather hasn't touched it.
bySkill.society: Always at head height, on walls a crowd faces, and never where the housing office would bother to paint over it. Whoever does this knows which walls nobody minds.
bySkill.survival: You read marks the way a tracker reads a trail. This one sits at eye height where people stop and stand, and you passed the same violet at the same height earlier today.

notes: Both checks cost nothing on any result.
